rule: A 2005 pick belongs to the club that held it on the symmetric league's activation date (2003-12-03): every real trade link dated before that day and not involving real Miami during the career applies (links before the career, such as Miami's pre-2003 deals, apply); links on or after it are real moves the simulated clubs did not make (docs/symmetric_league_design.md). Ownership is by the original club's pick, whatever slot the simulated lottery and records give it. A protected pick whose simulated slot falls inside its 2005 protection stays with the original club; the protection's later-year terms are recorded where sourced.
status: derived from Basketball-Reference team transaction pages 1997-98 to 2004-05 (every trade naming a 2005 first- or second-round pick), the Wikipedia 2005 draft footnotes and NBADraft.net's 2005 traded-picks list (protections)

forfeited.note: No 2005 pick was forfeited. Minnesota's 2000 salary-cap sanction took first-round picks in other years; Minnesota made its own 2005 first-round selection (BBR/Wikipedia 2005 draft).

expansion.note: Charlotte has no fixed slot in 2005: it enters the lottery as an ordinary non-playoff club, eligible for No. 1, and picks in round 2 by record (nba_2005_lottery_rules.json, charlotte_expansion). The 2004 keys are kept with null slots so a reader of the 2004 shape sees that no slot is reserved.

protection.2005: lottery-protected: Cleveland keeps the pick if it is a lottery club (picks 1-14)
protection.status: sourced (lottery protection, NBADraft.net 2005 traded picks: 'future Cleveland first-round pick (lottery protected)'); the terms after 2005 if the pick is not conveyed are unverified
protection.note: The protection was lifted on Feb 24, 2005 (Cleveland's Jiri Welsch trade), after activation, so it still applies in the simulation.

CLE.chain: CLE -> PHO (Oct 1, 1997, Antonio McDyess three-team trade with Denver). PHO -> CHA (June 22, 2004, for taking Jahidi White in the expansion draft) is after activation.

protection.status: sourced (NBADraft.net 2005 traded picks, describing the same Philadelphia pick: 'Protected through No. 8 in 2005, No. 5 in 2006 and unprotected in 2007')
protection.note: NBADraft.net states the terms for the pick as later held by Toronto; that they were unchanged from the Dec 18, 2002 Denver trade is derived (the later moves were straight assignments).

PHI.chain: PHI -> GSW (Oct 25, 2001, Derrick Coleman three-team trade); GSW -> PHI (June 26, 2002, Jiri Welsch); PHI -> DEN (Dec 18, 2002, Kenny Thomas / James Posey three-team trade). DEN -> NJN (July 15, 2004) and NJN -> TOR (Dec 17, 2004) are after activation.

protection.status: sourced (NBADraft.net 2005 traded picks: '2005 top 13 protected, 2006 top 3 protected, 2007 no protection')

WAS.chain: WAS -> ORL (Aug 1, 2001, Brendan Haywood trade). ORL -> DEN (June 24, 2004, Jameer Nelson) is after activation.

protection.status: sourced (NBADraft.net 2005 traded picks: 'a future Phoenix first-round pick (protected through 20th pick until 2008)'); what happens if it is not conveyed by 2008 is unverified

PHO.chain: PHO -> SAS (June 26, 2003, draft rights to Leandro Barbosa, made on the 2003 draft night that opens the career; it does not involve Miami). SAS -> NYK (Feb 25, 2005) is after activation.

ORL.chain: ORL -> TOR (Aug 3, 2000, Tracy McGrady sign-and-trade); TOR -> DET (Feb 22, 2001); DET -> ORL (June 2, 2001, three-team trade with Houston). Back with Orlando before activation.

CHI.chain: CHI -> PHO (June 24, 2004, Luol Deng; protected 1-3 in 2005 per NBADraft.net) is after activation.

DAL.chain: DAL -> UTA (June 24, 2004, Pavel Podkolzin) is after activation.

POR.chain: The Portland-Utah exchange of 2005 Nos. 3 and 6 (Utah also sent Dallas's No. 27 and a 2006 first) was made on draft day, June 28, 2005: after activation.

UTA.chain: See POR: the draft-day swap is after activation.

SAC.chain: SAC -> BOS (June 2003, draft rights to Darius Songaila; BBR dates it June 25, Wikipedia June 23).

HOU.chain: HOU -> NYK (June 11, 2003, compensation for coach Jeff Van Gundy). NYK -> PHO on draft night 2005 is after activation.

CHI.chain: CHI -> HOU (Sept 28, 2000, Bryce Drew); HOU -> UTA (Sept 30, 2003, John Amaechi / Glen Rice trade).

BOS.chain: BOS -> CLE (July 29, 2003, Jumaine Jones trade). CLE -> BOS (Dec 15, 2003, Ricky Davis / Tony Battie trade) is twelve days after activation, so Cleveland keeps it.

PHI.condition: Philadelphia owed Detroit one second-round pick of its choice from 2003-2005 (Dec 18, 1997, Theo Ratliff / Jerry Stackhouse trade). Its 2004 second-rounder already belonged to Atlanta (nba_2004_pick_ownership.json, round_2 PHI), so the obligation falls on the 2005 pick.
PHI.status: derived (BBR: 'Pick was PHI's choice of 2003-2005 2nd round picks'; that it was still outstanding at activation follows from its 2005 settlement). Philadelphia's real settlement with Phoenix's 2005 second-rounder, acquired June 7, 2005, is after activation.

LAC.condition: A conditional 2005 second-round swap or pick from the Nov 16, 2001 Bo Outlaw three-team trade (Clippers, Magic, Suns) was outstanding at activation. Sources disagree on its holder: BBR lists 'a 2005 2nd round draft pick' sent by the Clippers to Phoenix with no player selected and adds that Philadelphia had an option to swap with the Clippers in 2005 that it did not exercise; NBADraft.net says Orlando had the option to swap 2005 second-rounders with the Clippers. It was never exercised in reality.
LAC.status: unverified (holder and terms); recorded as not conveyed
LAC.chain: LAC -> NJN (July 29, 2004) and NJN -> GSW (Feb 14, 2005) are after activation.

PHO.chain: PHO -> UTA (Feb 19, 2004, Keon Clark / Tom Gugliotta) is after activation.

TOR.chain: Toronto and Orlando exchanged their 2005 second-rounders on Jan 2, 2004 (Robert Archibald trade): after activation.

CLE.chain: CLE -> ORL (July 23, 2004, Drew Gooden trade) is after activation.

MEM.chain: MEM -> SEA (June 24, 2004, Andre Emmett) is after activation.

MIA.chain: MIA -> TOR (June 24, 2004, Pape Sow / Albert Miralles) is a real Miami move after activation; never applied.

SAS.chain: SAS -> ATL (June 24, 2004, Viktor Sanikidze) is after activation.

CHA.chain: CHA -> LAC (July 14, 2004, Melvin Ely / Eddie House) is after activation.

notes.13: Cleveland's first belongs to Phoenix (1997) unless Cleveland is a lottery club; the Bobcats' acquisition (June 2004) and the lifting of the protection (Feb 2005) are after activation.
notes.16: Philadelphia's first belongs to Denver (Dec 2002), protected 1-8 in 2005.
notes.20: Washington's first belongs to Orlando (2001), protected 1-13 in 2005.
notes.30: Phoenix's first belongs to San Antonio (June 2003), protected 1-20 in 2005.
notes.50: Boston's second belongs to Cleveland: the July 29, 2003 trade is before activation and the Dec 15, 2003 return is after it.
notes.51: Chicago's second belongs to Utah via Houston (Sept 2003).
notes.54: Houston's second belongs to New York (Van Gundy compensation, June 2003).
notes.60: Philadelphia's own second goes to Detroit under the 1997 choice obligation (derived); the real substitution of Phoenix's pick is after activation.
notes.miami: No real Miami trade involving a 2005 pick falls between the career's start (2003-06-26) and activation; Miami holds both its own 2005 picks.
